winner.title: Peri Peri Chicken

evidence.authenticity: Butterflied whole bird, bird's eye chilli, garlic, lemon, vinegar, smoked paprika marinade, pan-drippings butter and brandy sauce, researched on a trip to Guia, Portugal. Page explains Portuguese explorers brought the chilli to Mozambique and that Southern Africa is the dish's origin. Author is Australian, not from the cuisine; roasted in the oven rather than charcoal.
evidence.precision: Grams for 6 of 18 ingredients (chicken 1.5 kg, salt 150 g, garlic 40 g, lemon 60 g, butter 50 g); oven 200C/400F; 60 min roast; brine ratio given; 15 min rest. No internal temperature, only time and appearance cues (blistered skin, juicy meat). Pan sizes vague (large baking tray). Small inconsistency: half vs three-quarters of the paste.
evidence.testing: Explains why for the brine (juicy breast), butterflying (faster, even skin coverage) and roasting over grilling (grill dries meat, roasting gives pan juices). 637 ratings averaging 5.
evidence.photos: Captioned step photos for cutting the backbone, flattening, coating underside and top, making the sauce, plus salad and chips. No photo of the roasting stage.
evidence.efficiency: Overnight brine plus 2 h marinade plus 1 h roast is long, though the reasons are given and most of it is hands-off. Sauce is made from drippings during the rest.
evidence.access: Bird's eye chillies are the only slightly hard item. No substitute is listed, but they are widely sold in US groceries and Asian markets.

winner.why: It has the most traditional flavor profile, with the best precision and reasoning, plus real process photos and a very large rating count, ahead of the NYT oven-roasted version.

runnerUp.title: Oven Roasted Peri Peri Chicken and Potatoes

evidence.authenticity: Kenyan-born author; intro states peri peri traces its origins to Mozambique, a former Portuguese colony, and notes the Swahili 'pili pili'. Uses Fresno chiles, oven and potatoes, so it is an adaptation of the traditionally grilled dish.
evidence.precision: Weights for chicken (3 lb) and potatoes (2 lb), 1/2-inch wedges, 450F oven, 35-45 min with cues (lightly browned, potatoes tender). Only 2 of 10 ingredients have weights; no tray size; no internal temperature.
evidence.testing: NYT test process, 210 ratings averaging 5, includes a tip on chiles.
evidence.photos: Page has many images, but step photos are hidden behind the login and could not be confirmed. Scored on that basis.
evidence.efficiency: About 1 h 15 min total, one tray, 30 min minimum marinade.
evidence.access: Fresno chiles and everything else are available at US groceries.

runnerUp.why: Fast and easy with a Mozambique-aware intro, but it has less precision, no confirmed process photos, and it swaps in Fresno chiles and potatoes.

notes: ATK version (Andrew Janjigian) is tested and precise (grill temperatures, 160F breast and 175F thigh) but takes five-spice and peanuts, is an African-inspired adaptation, and needs 6-24 h marinade. Immaculate Bites is the most explicitly Mozambican, but has weak precision and no step photos. TASTE/Nuno Mendes is Portuguese, with no internal temperature and no photos found; its pepper wording is inconsistent (cracked black vs white). Not scored in detail: Rick Stein, BBC Good Food and others in search results were not read. The winner is the Portuguese-style (Guia) preparation of a dish with Mozambican roots, so it is not a strictly Mozambican home recipe.
